answer.rationale:
The two symptoms this quarter are activation (-6%) and onboarding completion (-4%), which points at the top-of-funnel friction path rather than at price. Promotional pricing is the obvious reflex given the competitor's entry pricing, but memory_73 is the one inherited record with a full downstream readout, and it is explicitly negative: +31% activations and +18% revenue bought at -12pp renewal retention in exactly the SMB tier under attack. Discounting into a price war would buy borrowed activation against the primary objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue, so I am declining it despite it being the most situationally tempting option.

I intend simplify_onboarding because it is supported by two independent inherited records (memory_31 on signup field reduction, memory_86 on onboarding shortening) that map directly onto both degraded metrics, and because it addresses the competitor threat obliquely: lower friction narrows the effective cost of choosing us without touching price.

I am spending both verification pulls on memory_86 and memory_31 rather than on memory_73 precisely because those two are the load-bearing claims for the action I intend, and they are the least verified in the dimension that matters. Both are stated purely in early-funnel terms (activation lift, completion rate, time-to-value); neither reports renewal, expansion, or qualified-revenue outcomes. That is structurally the same shape as memory_73 before its retention cost showed up at renewal. memory_73 already carries its own downstream number, so pulling it would buy little. What I want from the archive is the measurement window and whether either study tracked accounts past first-week: if both stopped at week one, their 'durable lift' language is weaker than it reads and I should shrink scope.

Downstream risk I am flagging explicitly: cutting required signup fields can degrade lead qualification and routing data, which would quietly lower the quality of accounts entering the funnel even while activation counts rise. memory_44 suggests enterprise prospects need sales-assisted routing, and that routing depends on the very fields a simplification would remove. So the test must be scoped to the SMB self-serve path, must leave the enterprise demo-request path untouched, and must instrument renewal-cohort and qualified-pipeline metrics, not just completion.

Standard experiment scale with a long measurement window and pre-registered retention guardrails; not a broad rollout, because the durability of the inherited lift is exactly the thing not yet established. activation_messaging (memory_91) is my fallback if verification shows the onboarding records were short-window only.
